title: Soup at Camp
lines: The sun went down and camp got cold.
"Let us make soup for all of us," said Meg.
Meg and Sam got out a big black pot.
Mom set the pot on the camp fire.
Then she sat at the table to watch them.
Sam threw in beans, corn and nuts.
Meg cut a peach and a pear into bits.
"It needs juice next," said Meg to Tom.
Tom went to the shed to get the juice.
He came back and threw it all in.
Then the soup went blue!
"Why is my soup blue?" said Meg.
Sam had a good look in the jug.
It was not juice. It was blue glue.
Tom tried to spoon the glue back out.
But the blue had spread all the way down.
So the group had to start a new pot.
Mom gave them a clean pot and sat back down.
This time Meg read the jug first.
She let Tom mix the juice in with a spoon.
The new soup was good and hot.
They ate it all up under the stars.

questions.ask: What made the soup turn blue?
questions.listenFor: Blue glue that Tom threw in. Line fourteen says it.

questions.ask: What did Tom think he was putting in?
questions.listenFor: Juice. Line nine says he went to get the juice.

questions.ask: How could the kids keep this from happening again? Why?
questions.listenFor: Any sensible answer - read the jug, keep glue out of the camp pot. Listen for the reason.
